entry.title: How does the Omni Ring function in Pokemon Champions
entry.summary:
Upcoming title Pokémon Champions is still far away from its release, but we already know that the Omni Ring will be present.
The item is already on the game's official website, and it made the news during the 2025 World Championships final. It has already been confirmed that Pokémon Champions will be the official VGC software in Worlds 2026, and the Omni Ring will play an important role in the game.
How will the Omni Ring work in Pokémon Champions?
It's important to note that the Omni Ring's functions will only be clear once Pokémon Champions releases in 2026 (an exact release date remains unknown as of writing). However, we have official confirmation of its primary purpose: triggering mega evolutions during battles.
The item will be worn by trainers, enabling them to mega-evolve their Pokémon. In many ways, the Omni Ring is expected to work similarly to how the Mega Ring works in the mainline series.
Based on the current artwork of the ring, I expect the Omni Ring to have more functions. This will largely depend on the evolution features of the game. The Omni Ring may be used to enable features like Dynamax and perform Z-moves. Everything ultimately depends on the type of Pokémon we will get at launch, as not every creature can grow in battle with the help of the Dynamax ability.
Interestingly, the concept of mega evolutions has been making news a lot lately since the 2025 World Championships ended. While Pokémon Champions isn't coming out soon, Pokémon TCG Pocket is getting Mega Evolutions for the first time. The Company has confirmed that Mega Evolutions will be available in TCG Pocket during the Fall. How we will be able to mega evolve our Pokémon remains anyone's guess at this point.
One this is for sure that the Mega Evolutions will completely change the meta, but the extent is to be seen.

entry.title: Napoleonic France blends with Prototype in Ghostrunner dev’s new game—Valor Mortis
entry.summary:
Ghostrunner devs have just announced their new game, Valor Mortis, set in Napoleonic France and featuring a lot of Prototype- and Resident Evil-inspired madness. Information is still scarce, but the reveal trailer certainly had a lot to say.
During the gamescom 2025 pre-show event, we got to see a ton of new games, primarily from smaller studios and indie developers. One of them particularly caught my eye, though—Valor Mortis, a title developed by the same team behind the stellar first-person action series Ghostrunner.
It is set during Napoleonic times, line warfare, winter, and all, but features a monstrous twist straight out of Prototype. The characters turn into grotesque creatures and gain insidious powers after consuming a strange fluid, much like infestation and viruses provide powers in Prototype and Resident Evil. The player, too, makes use of these powers as well, so it's not something limited to NPCs.
It's a first-person title with what appears to be grounded, meaty combat, alongside stomach-churning fun.
It's also coming in 2026 to Xbox Series X and S, and hopefully other platforms down the line.
This is a developing story, with more to come as information becomes available.

entry.title: Rusticl vs. AMD ROCm Performance On Ryzen AI Max+ "Strix Halo"
entry.summary: One of the set of tests I have been meaning to carry out for a number of months has been comparing the Mesa Rusticl performance to different dedicated hardware drivers. Rusticl is the Rust-based OpenCL 3.0 driver within Mesa that works across Gallium3D drivers and over the past many months has been maturing rather well. Among the targets I have been wanting to compare is how well Rusticl competes with the AMD ROCm OpenCL implementation for Radeon GPUs. Given all the interest recently around Strix Halo and the Framework Desktop as well, today's benchmarking is looking at the performance between these different OpenCL driver implementations for the Radeon 8060S Graphics.

entry.title: All EA FC 25 Pre-Season Transfer Update objective rewards and tasks
entry.summary:
The Pre-Season Transfer Update objective has been released in EA FC 25, and it's a surprising set of tasks that you can complete to get up to two FUTTIES items.
The objective, released on Monday evening, includes a set of simple tasks that can be completed in Ultimate Team. The central theme of the objective revolves around cards of footballers who have made a switch in the summer transfer window.
Let's take a look at how to complete all the tasks, along with the rewards on offer.
EA FC 25 Pre-Season Transfer Update objective guide
The Pre-Season Transfer Update has five tasks to complete.
Task How to Complete Rewards
Score 5 Score 5 goals with a Power Shot in one Squad Battles match on Semi-Pro difficulty. 83+ Rare Gold Players Pack (10)
Win 3 Win 3 Rush matches. 84+ Rare Gold Players Pack (7)
Score 10 Score 10 goals from outside of the box in Squad Battles matches on Amateur difficulty. Evan Ferguson FUTTIES
Score 3 Score 3 goals with a Finesse Shot in one Squad Battles match on Professional difficulty. 88+ Rare Gold Players Pack
Win 2 Win 2 Rivals matches. 86+ Rare Gold Players Pack (3)
If you manage to score 10 goals in Squad Battles on Amateur, you get to pick Evan Ferguson FUTTIES. The 97-rated card has decent stats, but the task can be quite boring. I am more excited about the reward you get for completing the full set.
The complete set rewards you with a 97-rated Joao Pedro FUTTIES item. The Brazilian, who recently made his summer switch to Chelsea, receives a special card as part of the FUTTIES promo. The packs you get can always land you with a 99-rated FUTTIES item from the Pre-Season Re-Release Batch 3 if you're lucky enough. The batch includes over 260 special cards from older promos and FUTTIES, and there are a few 99-rated cards in the mix as well.

entry.title: Gimmicks are god in Psycutlery, a delightful free spork-driven platformer from the creator of Psycho Waluigi
entry.summary:
The curse of plausibility and coherence lies heavy across this realism-centred artform. These days, you can't even give a platform character a woolly hat without first devising an in-game textile industry with appropriate supply chains, and a whole supporting cast of millworkers with names like Arthur Worsted and Jimmy Shuttlecock. I prefer the disconnectedness of Psycutlery, in which you fight using a telekinetic spork, buy things with frogspawn, heal by eating toothpaste, and checkpoint progress by carving blocks of stone into statues of yourself, using the spork. The in-game reasoning for all this is basically "because developer Luke Tarlowe has the imagination of a Picasso and the attention span of a goldfish". Don't call it CRAZY. Call it refreshingly uninhibited and also, reminiscent of, Decap Attack and Ristar. Also, call it free.

entry.title: Piracy Shield Widens Scope to Protect Movie & TV Premieres & Live Music
entry.summary: After focusing on IPTV services offering pirated live football matches from Italy's Serie A, legal amendments adopted by telecoms regulator AGCOM last week will widen the scope of the Piracy Shield blocking platform. entry.title: Canadian Court Rejects Reverse Class Action Lawsuit Against BitTorrent Pirates
entry.summary: After years of legal skirmishes, an ambitious strategy by film studio Voltage Pictures, to sue alleged BitTorrent pirates through a reverse class action in Canada, has been permanently shut down. The Federal Court of Appeal ruled that these cases, where IP addresses are the main initial evidence, are unsuited to this legal approach. Furthermore, the proposed methods for mass notification are deemed unlawful. From: TF, for the latest news on copyright battles, piracy and more.
